title: Confirm Regressions, Revert Harmful Changes, and Verify Recovery

story.so_that: flaky evidence cannot discard useful work and confirmed harmful changes cannot leave the repository degraded
story.i_want: an apparently worse candidate re-evaluated unchanged, a confirmed regression reverted, and the restored accepted state verified before refinement continues

journey.before: A candidate evaluation is observed to perform worse than the current best accepted state
journey.during: Re-evaluate the unchanged candidate, classify the combined evidence, revert on confirmed regression, and rerun the suite to verify recovery
journey.after: Autonomous refinement continues from a verified restored state, or the evidence is handed off to a human without further autonomous mutation

capability_breakdown.core_action: Re-evaluate an unchanged candidate that performed worse than the current best accepted state, classify the combined evidence as confirmed regression, unstable result, suspected flakiness, or inconclusive, revert the repository on confirmed regression, rerun the suite to verify recovery, and preserve reverted-proposal context for future planning before allowing the next proposal.
inputs: Current best accepted-state metrics and repository revision
Change summary for the reverted proposal
Recovery evaluation results for the restored state
Consecutive confirmed-regression counter and durable progress history
outputs: Recorded degraded evidence and change summary
Retained reverted-proposal context for future planning
state_changes: Consecutive confirmed-regression counter is incremented on confirmed regression
Repository is reset to the last accepted state on confirmed regression
Degraded evidence, confirmation result, and recovery result are recorded in durable history
Reverted-proposal context remains visible for future planning

ui: Regression confirmation and re-evaluation status view
Human handoff notification and recovery result view
api: Regression classification and evidence recording endpoint
Repository revert and accepted-state restore endpoint
database: Best accepted state and metrics tracking
Consecutive-regression counter and durable progress history
Degraded evidence and reverted-proposal context store
external_services: Version control system for revert and restore operations
Evaluation provider or runner for re-evaluation and recovery

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a second evaluation run against the unchanged candidate also performs worse than the current best state, when the regression is confirmed, then both degraded results and the change summary are recorded, the consecutive-regression counter increments, the last accepted state is restored, and the suite is rerun to verify recovery.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a second evaluation run against the unchanged candidate also performs worse than the current best state when the regression is confirmed then both degraded results and the change summary are recorded the consecutive-regression counter increments the last accepted state is restored and the suite is rerun to verify recovery
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Confirm and recover from a harmful change

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the second evaluation run returns to or exceeds the current best state, when results are compared, then the result is treated as unstable, a human is notified, and no autonomous commit or revert decision is made.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the second evaluation run returns to or exceeds the current best state when results are compared then the result is treated as unstable a human is notified and no autonomous commit or revert decision is made
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Escalate unstable evidence to a human

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the second evaluation run errors, times out, or otherwise fails to establish stable equivalence, improvement, or regression, when results are classified, then the evidence is recorded as suspected flakiness, a human is notified, and autonomous refinement does not continue.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the second evaluation run errors times out or otherwise fails to establish stable equivalence improvement or regression when results are classified then the evidence is recorded as suspected flakiness a human is notified and autonomous refinement does not continue
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Escalate inconclusive evidence to a human

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a confirmed regression has been reverted, when the recovery evaluation runs, then it must demonstrate that the restored accepted state matches its previously recorded performance before another proposal is allowed.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a confirmed regression has been reverted when the recovery evaluation runs then it must demonstrate that the restored accepted state matches its previously recorded performance before another proposal is allowed
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Verify the restored accepted state matches prior performance

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the recovery evaluation cannot verify the restored performance, when recovery fails, then autonomous refinement stops and hands off to a human.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the recovery evaluation cannot verify the restored performance when recovery fails then autonomous refinement stops and hands off to a human
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Stop and escalate when recovery fails

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a proposal is reverted, when it is recorded, then its change summary, affected files, rationale, observed degradation, confirmation result, and recovery result remain visible to future planning steps.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a proposal is reverted when it is recorded then its change summary affected files rationale observed degradation confirmation result and recovery result remain visible to future planning steps
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Preserve reverted proposal context for future planning

edge_cases.criterion: Second evaluation produces identical metrics to the first worse run
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the unchanged candidate re-evaluation produces metrics identical to the first worse run when the classification runs then the regression is confirmed and the revert path proceeds

edge_cases.criterion: Second evaluation returns exactly to the current best state
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the second evaluation run returns exactly to the current best state when results are compared then the result is classified as unstable and escalated to a human
edge_cases.jtbd: Treat equal results as unstable evidence

edge_cases.criterion: Second evaluation errors or times out
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the second evaluation run errors or exceeds the configured timeout when classification runs then the evidence is recorded as suspected flakiness and a human is notified
edge_cases.jtbd: Handle re-evaluation failure without false regression

edge_cases.criterion: Evaluation provider or configuration changes between first and second run
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the evaluation provider or configuration differs from the original evaluation when the second run is attempted then the workflow records the deviation and retries with the original configuration

edge_cases.criterion: Current best accepted state is missing or corrupted
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the current best accepted state metrics or revision cannot be found when the comparison runs then the workflow records the missing state and hands off to a human
edge_cases.jtbd: Avoid automated decisions without a valid baseline

edge_cases.criterion: Repository reset fails after regression confirmation
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the repository revert fails after a regression is confirmed when the restore attempt completes then the workflow records the failure and stops for human intervention

edge_cases.criterion: Recovery evaluation shows a different result from the previously recorded best state
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the recovery evaluation does not reproduce the previously recorded accepted state performance when the recovery result is classified then the workflow stops and escalates to a human
Given the human notification channel is unavailable when the workflow must hand off then the workflow records the handoff and retries notification according to policy

edge_cases.criterion: Reverted proposal spans many files or multiple commits
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a reverted proposal affects many files or multiple commits when the revert is applied then all affected files and commit references are recorded for future planning

edge_cases.criterion: Consecutive regression counter is already at a stop threshold
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the consecutive confirmed-regression counter is already at a stop threshold when a new regression is confirmed then the workflow records the threshold and stops for human review

questions.question: How is the second unchanged-candidate evaluation invoked and guaranteed to use the exact same code, configuration, and provider as the first evaluation?
What is the exact classification logic for distinguishing confirmed regression, unstable result, suspected flakiness, and inconclusive evidence?
How is the last accepted repository state identified and restored safely, including any uncommitted or staged changes?
What matching criteria does the recovery evaluation use to verify the restored state matches its previously recorded performance?
How is reverted-proposal context structured and linked to future planning steps?
What human handoff path and notification content are used for unstable, flaky, inconclusive, and failed recovery outcomes?

in_sprint_assumptions: The blocked-by stories 'Initialize a run, establish a baseline, and plan refinement' and 'Evaluate candidates, advance the quality ratchet, and finalize the run' are available before implementation.
Version control, evaluation provider, and notification services are provisioned and accessible.
The classification rules for regression, unstable, flaky, and inconclusive evidence are defined before the classification service is implemented.
The recovery-evaluation tolerance and success criteria are agreed upon before verification logic is implemented.
